headline: LongChang tests free exploration for evidence-supported discovery in simulated physics
summary: The LongChang preprint reports a benchmark for whether language models can notice unexpected behavior in simulated physical worlds, choose questions and test altered physical laws without assigned research tasks or hints. Across 12 models and 15 fixed-start MuJoCo scenes, the authors report a 16.7% discovery rate for GPT-6-Astra and 0% for the other 11 models; discovery required both correct law identification and evidence support. In the ordinary-physics control, 36.1% of reports were rejected for false anomalies or unsupported explanations. GPT-6.1-Sol judged reports and GPT-6-Astra reviewed apparatus and generated/reviewed evolved scenes. These are author-reported results in a bounded simulation, not evidence of general scientific autonomy or real-world discovery.
